title: Binary Logistic Regression from Scratch via Batch Gradient Descent
description: Generate two 2D Gaussian clusters, minimize binary cross-entropy loss with logistic_gd on X_aug, and plot the log-loss convergence curve and probability contour map.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Sample points from `mean0 = [0, 0]` (`class 0`) and `mean1 = [2, 2]` (`class 1`) using the supplied counts and shared covariance `cov`. Stack them into `X_bin` and `y_bin`, and shuffle with `np.random.permutation(n)`.
Define `sigmoid(z)`, `logistic_loss(theta, X, y)`, and `logistic_gd` with the supplied defaults. Each gradient step computes `grad = X.T @ (p - y) / len(y)` and updates `theta -= lr * grad`.

Look at lines 28-32: each gradient descent step computes predicted probabilities `p = sigmoid(X @ theta)` and forms the residual vector `p - y`. It projects that vector onto `X.T / len(y)` and appends the updated `logistic_loss` to `history`.

steps.question: Why does line 22 add the supplied eps inside `np.log(p + eps)` and `np.log(1 - p + eps)`?
steps.answer: Adding eps prevents `np.log(0)` (`-inf` or `nan`) if a predicted probability `p` ever rounds to zero or one.

steps.description: Prepend a column of ones to form `X_aug`. Run `logistic_gd` on `X_aug` and `y_bin` with the supplied settings to reach `Final loss: 0.28075158713736514`. Plot both `hist` and the 2D probability contours `probs = sigmoid(grid @ theta).reshape(xx.shape)`.
